title: Paridyum Tool Registry
description: Every tool the estate installs, pins, or depends on the behaviour of, declared under ADR-0066. This registry owns ADOPTION facts — purpose, licence, source, exit path, and the artifact that decided it — and owns NO version number where another file already holds one. An entry pinned in toolchain-registry.yaml carries `pin_home` and no version; RFC-0015 gives a fact one home and a version copied here is that rule broken sideways. Validated by `knowledge.tool_registry_valid`.

version.description: Registry format version. Bump only for a breaking shape change, which needs an ADR.

tools.description: One entry per tool, sorted by id ascending so diffs stay readable. Uniqueness of `id` is enforced by the gate, not expressible here.

id.description: The invocable name, lowercase. `gh`, `jq`, `archify`, `talosctl`. The name a script actually types, not a product name — a registry keyed on marketing is a registry nobody greps.

name.description: The product name, when it differs from the invocable id. Omit when they match.

purpose.description: One sentence: what the estate uses it FOR. The same role `provides` plays in a manifest under STD-0013 — the field a future reader needs before they rebuild a capability that already exists. Not a description of the tool; a description of our use of it.

licence.description: SPDX identifier where one applies, or `proprietary`, or `service` for a hosted dependency with terms rather than a licence. REQ-0012's exitability test starts here and ADR-0052 names skipping it as the characteristic drift.

source.description: Where it comes from — the canonical repository or vendor URL. The thing to read when the pin needs advancing or the project is abandoned.

tier.description: REQ-0012 §5 criticality. `critical` = the estate cannot operate without it. `supporting` = its loss degrades or blocks a workflow but is survivable within a day. `convenience` = a nicer way to do something that is possible without it. The tier is a judgement made on the day of adoption, which is why `exit` is required at every tier and not only at `critical`.

adopted_by.description: The artifact id(s) that decided or record this adoption. ADR-0066 decision 6: a tool with no artifact behind it is a decision nobody made. Where the tool predates its artifact, this names the artifact that RECORDS it and `notes` says the adoption was retrospective — recorded rather than backdated.

install.description: How a clean workstation gets it, pinned. Omit only for a tool the platform ships with or that another registry's pin already installs — in which case `pin_home` says where.

method.description: The install mechanism. `git` means clone at a sha, which is the only method available for a package that is not published anywhere.

ref.description: The immutable reference: a 40-character commit sha, a signed tag, or an exact package version. Never a branch, never `latest`, never absent. `knowledge.declared_tool_install_is_pinned` rejects a mutable ref — an unpinned install recorded in a registry is worse than no registry, because it reports the dependency as governed.

ref_dated.description: When the ref was set. A pin with no date is a pin nobody dares advance — the lesson toolchain-registry.yaml records about 1.90.0.

path.description: The entrypoint within the installed tree, when it is not the tool's own name on PATH.

pin_home.description: Names the file or system that already owns this tool's version, when one does. `toolchain-registry` means the number lives in toolchain-registry.yaml under some stack's `tooling:` key. An entry with `pin_home` MUST NOT carry `install.ref` — that is two homes for one fact, and `knowledge.tool_registry_holds_no_version` rejects it.

exit.description: REQ-0012 §5. What is lost if this tool disappears, what replaces it, and roughly how long that takes. Prose, because none of those three is enumerable. Required at every tier: an exit plan written after the dependency is load-bearing is written under pressure and is usually fiction.

network.description: Whether the tool reaches the network in normal operation. `none` = never. `explicit` = only under a command the operator names. `always` = it is a client for something remote. REQ-0012 §4 wants an egress allowlist and REQ-0007 §4 names egress as the strongest available mitigation for prompt injection; neither can be built without this field.

declared.description: When the entry was added here. Not when the tool was adopted — `adopted_by` carries that, and the gap between the two dates is the honest record of how late this registry arrived.

notes.description: What a future reader would otherwise reconstruct expensively: why this one and not the obvious alternative, what is known-bad about it, whether the entry is retrospective. STD-0011 is the rule; this is the field.
